name: blueprint/document-action-plan
description: Turn a document or meeting note into a plan that acts (Hermes document-to-action-items / meeting-action-items, righthand-native): rh_text_extract pulls cited obligations with owners and deadlines, each becomes a task AND a reminder, and the reminder delivers through ntfy when its time comes.
use_cases: what did this contract obligate us to do
meeting notes to owners and tickets
ingredients: rh_text_extract with an obligations schema (cite + action + owner + deadline)
rh_task_create per action (typed board, open -> done/failed)
rh_events_due each turn + rh_notify_send for the delivery
recipe: extract: rh_text_extract { text, schema: { obligations: [{ cite, action, owner, deadline }] } } -> board: rh_task_create per obligation, the cite in the detail -> schedule: rh_events_create per deadline (at = the ISO deadline, title = the action) -> each turn rh_events_due returns what has come due and marks it notified -> rh_notify_send the due items -> when the task is done, cancel or complete both halves
result_kind: one task + one event per obligation, receipts on delivery

invoke_contract.extract: { text, schema } -> { obligations: [{ cite, action, owner, deadline }] }

cost_hint: one model call per extraction; tasks/events/notify free
pitfalls: every obligation keeps its cite - an action without the sentence that spawned it is unfalsifiable
extract is schema-in, object-out; a malformed deadline fails the call cleanly, do not half-board
the task and the event are two halves: the board tracks the work, the event delivers the interruption - complete both
due marks notified at return time: exactly-once delivery is the state flip, not caller discipline
the model hallucinating an obligation is the failure mode - the cite is what lets the user check
local_limits: reminders fire only on turns the agent runs
cloud_limits: cron escalation for the due check (documented); the extraction stays a single LLM call
